facts.raw_span: subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
Cell differential: 1% lymphocytes, 1% monocytes/macrophages, 98% atypical cells/blasts

concepts.why: The patient has violaceous cutaneous lesions consistent with leukemia cutis and a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis.

The patient has a high white blood cell count, a high percentage of atypical cells/blasts, and a significant number of red blood cells in the cerebrospinal fluid analysis, consistent with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, consistent with neurolymphomatosis.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, consistent with CNS lymphoma.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, consistent with Guillain-Barre syndrome.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and reduced muscle stretch reflexes, consistent with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
The patient has multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion and a high white blood cell count, consistent with multiple myeloma.
The patient has multiple areas of cutaneous scalp demonstrated restriction of diffusion and a high white blood cell count, consistent with plasma cell neoplasm.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, consistent with lymphomatous meningitis.
The patient has severe flaccid quadriparesis and nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots, consistent with leptomeningeal metastasis.

rationales.F01: Subacute progressive weakness is more typical of leukemia or lymphoma than Guillain-Barre Syndrome or CIDP.
rationales.F04: Severe flaccid quadriparesis is highly suggestive of a severe neurological condition such as leukemia or lymphoma.
rationales.F06: Violaceous cutaneous lesions are highly suggestive of leukemia cutis, which is a strong indicator of leukemia.
rationales.F09: Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots is highly suggestive of neurolymphomatosis or lymphomatous meningitis.
rationales.F11: A cell differential with 98% atypical cells/blasts is highly suggestive of leukemia or lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: High white blood cell count, presence of atypical cells/blasts in cerebrospinal fluid, and violaceous cutaneous lesions support Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia as the most specific diagnosis.
